boards.title: 10 Late-Night Runs That Explain Moravian University
boards.description: Current late-night destinations in Bethlehem, including campus spaces and food counters with publicly posted hours.

cards.title: Haupert Union Building
cards.subtitle: Moravian University Main Street Campus, Bethlehem
cards.notes: Use the HUB for a campus-based evening stop; check its event calendar and building access before heading over.
cards.short_summary: Moravian’s campus union stays open through 11 p.m. most nights and midnight on Fridays and Saturdays.
cards.evidence_claim: Moravian lists HUB academic-year hours until 11 p.m. Monday–Thursday and Sunday, and until midnight Friday and Saturday.
cards.access_notes: Academic-year hours: Mon–Thu 6 a.m.–11 p.m.; Fri 6 a.m.–midnight; Sat 7 a.m.–midnight; Sun 8 a.m.–11 p.m.

cards.title: Reeves Library
cards.subtitle: Moravian University Main Street Campus, Bethlehem
cards.notes: Plan a focused study stop during the regular academic year, and confirm holiday, break, and summer changes first.
cards.short_summary: A campus study destination with published midnight closing on several regular-term nights.
cards.evidence_claim: Moravian’s Student Affairs handbook lists Reeves Library open until midnight Sunday and Monday through Thursday during the regular academic year.
cards.access_notes: Regular academic-year hours listed: Sun 1 p.m.–midnight; Mon–Thu 8 a.m.–midnight. The handbook says hours can change for breaks, holidays, and summer.

cards.title: Taco Bell on East Fourth Street
cards.subtitle: 1620 East Fourth Street, Bethlehem
cards.notes: Use the drive-thru when dining room service has ended; review the location page for the nightly schedule before leaving.
cards.short_summary: A Bethlehem Taco Bell location with drive-thru service posted until 1 a.m. daily.
cards.evidence_claim: Taco Bell lists drive-thru hours of 9 a.m.–1 a.m. every day for its 1620 East Fourth Street Bethlehem location.
cards.source_title: Taco Bell, 1620 East Fourth Street | Official location page
cards.access_notes: Posted drive-thru hours are 9 a.m.–1 a.m. daily; posted dine-in hours end earlier, at 10 p.m.

cards.title: Taco Bell on Easton Avenue
cards.subtitle: 2585 Easton Avenue, Bethlehem
cards.notes: Choose the drive-thru for the late window and check the store page on the day of your visit for any changes.
cards.short_summary: A second Bethlehem Taco Bell with a separately listed late drive-thru schedule.
cards.evidence_claim: Taco Bell lists drive-thru hours of 9 a.m.–1 a.m. every day for its 2585 Easton Avenue Bethlehem location.
cards.source_title: Taco Bell, 2585 Easton Avenue | Official location page
cards.access_notes: Posted drive-thru hours are 9 a.m.–1 a.m. daily; posted dine-in hours end earlier, at 10 p.m.

cards.title: Pizza Hut on Easton Avenue
cards.subtitle: 1314 Easton Avenue, Bethlehem
cards.notes: Use the official ordering page to select carryout or delivery, then verify the midnight closing shown for this location.
cards.short_summary: This Pizza Hut’s official Bethlehem listing posts service until midnight.
cards.evidence_claim: Pizza Hut’s Bethlehem location page lists the 1314 Easton Avenue restaurant as open until midnight.
cards.source_title: Pizza Delivery & Carryout in Bethlehem, PA | Pizza Hut
cards.access_notes: The official location listing identifies 1314 Easton Ave and says it is open until midnight; confirm ordering availability before departing.

cards.title: Wendy’s on Broadway Street
cards.subtitle: 308 Broadway Street, Bethlehem
cards.notes: Check the location page’s day-specific listing, then use the posted late closing window for a food pickup or drive-thru stop.
cards.short_summary: A South Bethlehem Wendy’s location whose official listing includes a 2 a.m. closing day.
cards.evidence_claim: Wendy’s official Bethlehem directory lists its 308 Broadway Street location and shows one day open until 2 a.m.
cards.access_notes: The official directory lists 308 Broadway St and shows a day-specific closing time of 2 a.m.; verify the current day’s hours before going.

cards.title: Haaz’s Bethlehem
cards.subtitle: 3217 Schoenersville Road, Bethlehem
cards.notes: Place a pickup order through the restaurant’s official ordering page and use the posted weekend window when it applies.
cards.short_summary: A fast-casual Bethlehem restaurant with official ordering hours extending to 2 a.m. on Friday and Saturday.
cards.evidence_claim: Haaz’s official Toast page lists hours until midnight Sunday–Thursday and until 2 a.m. Friday and Saturday.
cards.access_notes: Posted hours: 10 a.m.–midnight Sun–Thu and 10 a.m.–2 a.m. Fri–Sat.

cards.title: The Market Gourmet Express
cards.subtitle: Wind Creek Outlets, 77 Wind Creek Boulevard, Bethlehem
cards.notes: Enter through the Outlets or hotel as directed for minors, then check the listed counter hours before making the trip.
cards.short_summary: An outlet-area food hall with several counters open late, including some with 24-hour schedules.
cards.evidence_claim: Wind Creek says minors may dine at The Market when entering through The Outlets or hotel, and lists late and 24-hour counter schedules.
cards.source_title: The Market Gourmet Express | Wind Creek Bethlehem
cards.access_notes: Minors are directed to enter through The Outlets or hotel. The page lists South Philly Steaks & Fries as open 24 hours Wed–Sun and other late counters.

cards.title: Mo’ Burger at The Market
cards.subtitle: Wind Creek Outlets, 77 Wind Creek Boulevard, Bethlehem
cards.notes: Enter through the Outlets or hotel if under 21, and confirm whether the late Friday–Saturday counter schedule is in effect.
cards.short_summary: A Market counter with posted service to 2 a.m. on Friday and Saturday.
cards.evidence_claim: Wind Creek lists Mo’ Burger at The Market open 7 a.m.–midnight Sunday–Thursday and 7 a.m.–2 a.m. Friday–Saturday.
cards.source_title: The Market Gourmet Express | Wind Creek Bethlehem
cards.access_notes: For minors, Wind Creek directs entry through The Outlets or hotel. Mo’ Burger’s listed late window is Fri–Sat until 2 a.m.

cards.title: South Philly Steaks & Fries at The Market
cards.subtitle: Wind Creek Outlets, 77 Wind Creek Boulevard, Bethlehem
cards.notes: Use the outlet or hotel entry route for minors and confirm the weekday schedule before relying on the overnight counter.
cards.short_summary: A Market counter with official 24-hour service posted from Wednesday through Sunday.
cards.evidence_claim: Wind Creek lists South Philly Steaks & Fries at The Market open 10 a.m.–midnight Monday–Tuesday and 24 hours Wednesday–Sunday.
cards.source_title: The Market Gourmet Express | Wind Creek Bethlehem
cards.access_notes: For minors, Wind Creek directs entry through The Outlets or hotel. South Philly Steaks & Fries is listed open 24 hours Wed–Sun.

boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Ten named Moravian spaces for studying, creating, meeting, attending events, and recreation across the North and South campuses.

cards.title: Set up at Reeves Library
cards.subtitle: North Campus · Locust and Monocacy Streets
cards.notes: Choose a carrel, lounge seat, group area, or study room; use the lower-level movable furniture and whiteboards to shape a project session.
cards.short_summary: A library with room for quiet work, group work, and research help.
cards.evidence_claim: Moravian says Reeves Library offers study tables, individual carrels, group areas, lounge seating, study rooms, and lower-level movable furniture and whiteboards.
cards.access_notes: Library access and hours may vary by academic term; check Reeves Library before visiting.

cards.title: Make media in the Zinzenko Center
cards.subtitle: Lower level of Reeves Library
cards.notes: Reserve or coordinate use of the study lounge and recording studios when a class project needs audio, video, or a collaborative editing setup.
cards.short_summary: A Reeves Library media-creation and study lounge space.
cards.evidence_claim: Moravian identifies the Zinzenko New Media Center as a Reeves Library space with a study lounge plus video and audio recording studios.
cards.source_title: Reeves Library Home Page | Moravian University
cards.access_notes: Listed as reservable through the library’s room-booking service; confirm availability before planning a session.

cards.title: Meet up at the HUB
cards.subtitle: North Campus · student center
cards.notes: Use the student-center building as a starting point for a meeting, campus event, dining stop, or visit to student-life and organization offices.
cards.short_summary: Moravian’s central student-center building for collaboration, events, and campus services.
cards.evidence_claim: Moravian describes the HUB as centralizing programs and resources for students and as a space for collaboration, meetings, and events.
cards.source_title: Celebrating the Haupert Union Building | Moravian University
cards.access_notes: Building spaces and services have their own schedules and reservation requirements.

cards.title: Catch a large event in the Pavilion
cards.subtitle: Haupert Union Building · dining and multipurpose room
cards.notes: Check the campus calendar for programs held here; the room operates as a dining room and converts for large-scale campus events.
cards.short_summary: A HUB dining room that also hosts large campus programs.
cards.evidence_claim: Moravian states that the Pavilion is a dining room and multipurpose space for many large-scale events on campus.
cards.access_notes: Dining and event access depends on the current schedule; verify the event details or dining availability.

cards.title: Look for a speaker or performance at Prosser
cards.subtitle: Haupert Union Building
cards.notes: Use the event calendar to find a guest speaker or small performance, then confirm whether the specific program is open to attendees.
cards.short_summary: A 275-capacity HUB event space for speakers and small performances.
cards.evidence_claim: Moravian describes Prosser Auditorium as a 275-person event space suited to guest speakers and small performances.
cards.access_notes: Event admission and availability are determined by each program.

cards.title: Pause on the HUB Portico
cards.subtitle: Behind the Haupert Union Building · overlooking Makuvek Field
cards.notes: Use the covered outdoor overlook as a brief between-class stop, especially when an activity or game is taking place on Makuvek Field.
cards.short_summary: A covered HUB overlook facing Makuvek Field.
cards.evidence_claim: Moravian identifies the Portico as a HUB space at the back of the building that overlooks Makuvek Field.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor access may be affected by weather or scheduled events.

cards.title: Watch or join activity at Makuvek Field
cards.subtitle: Main Street Campus · North Campus
cards.notes: Check recreation and athletics schedules for field activity; the central field hosts several varsity teams as well as intramural sports and other activities.
cards.short_summary: A central North Campus field used for varsity and intramural activity.
cards.evidence_claim: Moravian says John Makuvek Field is home to field hockey, lacrosse, and soccer, plus a variety of intramural sports and other activities.
cards.source_title: Brilliant Students and Athletes | Moravian University
cards.access_notes: Field use is scheduled; participate only through the relevant team, club, or recreation program.

cards.title: Work out at the Fitness Center
cards.subtitle: Breidegam Field House · North Campus
cards.notes: Bring your Moravian ID and choose cardio, strength, free-weight, or core equipment; the facility is open to students, faculty, and staff.
cards.short_summary: A 10,000-square-foot campus workout space inside Breidegam Field House.
cards.evidence_claim: Moravian states that its Fitness Center in Breidegam Field House is open to all students, faculty, and staff and includes cardio equipment and weight areas.
cards.source_title: New Student Guide to Campus Life | Moravian University
cards.access_notes: Bring a valid Moravian ID and check the fitness center’s current operating hours before visiting.

cards.title: Bring a draft to the Writing Center
cards.subtitle: Second floor of Zinzendorf Hall
cards.notes: Reserve an in-person appointment for feedback on anything from rough notes to a finished draft; ask about a Zinzendorf Hall or Reeves Library meeting.
cards.short_summary: Peer writing support for projects at any stage of development.
cards.evidence_claim: Moravian says the Writing Center is on Zinzendorf Hall’s second floor, staffed by trained Moravian students, and supports writing from rough notes through finished drafts.
cards.access_notes: Appointments are recommended; walk-ins are accommodated when possible.

cards.title: Book a quantitative-support session
cards.subtitle: Third floor of the Sally Breidegam Miksiewicz Center for Health Sciences
cards.notes: Book ahead when you want one-on-one or small-group peer tutoring for an introductory math or quantitative course; bring the assignment or questions.
cards.short_summary: A peer-tutoring space for Moravian’s 100-level math and quantitative courses.
cards.evidence_claim: Moravian states that the Quantitative Resource Center offers individual and small-group assistance from trained undergraduate peer tutors for 100-level math and quantitative courses.
cards.access_notes: Use Moravian’s WConline scheduling platform to review availability and book in advance.

boards.title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
boards.description: Ten documented no-cost activities and destinations in Bethlehem, with eligibility and scheduling notes included where applicable.

cards.title: Join Fitness in the Garden
cards.subtitle: Bethlehem Rose Garden
cards.notes: Register for a monthly outdoor class, complete the required waiver, and use the provided equipment or bring a mat. Check the seasonal schedule first.
cards.short_summary: A city-run outdoor fitness class at the Rose Garden.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Bethlehem identifies Fitness in the Garden as a free program for all, held monthly from April through September.
cards.access_notes: Seasonal; registration and a waiver are required. The city recommends the program for ages 16 and older; minors need a parent or guardian.

cards.title: Walk Monocacy Way on Trail Tuesday
cards.subtitle: Meet at Memorial Pool, 259 Illick's Mill Road
cards.notes: Join the scheduled guided walk at the Memorial Pool meeting point. Review the activity topic and complete the city waiver before heading out.
cards.short_summary: A guided Trail Tuesday walk on Monocacy Way.
cards.evidence_claim: The city lists a Trail Tuesday walk on the Monocacy Way Trail and states Trail Tuesday is free for all residents.
cards.access_notes: Seasonal first-Tuesday program, April through October; waiver required. The city specifies it is free for residents, and minors need a parent or guardian.

cards.title: Take a D&L Trail Tuesday outing
cards.subtitle: Meet at the Ice House, 56 River Street
cards.notes: Choose a listed walk or bike ride, meet at the Ice House, and bring a helmet if joining a bike activity. Confirm the current schedule beforehand.
cards.short_summary: A city-led walk, ride, or history outing on the D&L Trail.
cards.evidence_claim: The city schedules Trail Tuesday birdwatching, bike, and history activities on the D&L Trail and states the program is free for all residents.
cards.access_notes: Seasonal first-Tuesday program, April through October; waiver required. The city specifies it is free for residents; helmets are required on bike rides.

cards.title: Walk the South Bethlehem Greenway
cards.subtitle: Meet at Harmony Pavilion on the Greenway
cards.notes: Use the Harmony Pavilion meeting point between Webster and Taylor streets for the scheduled guided walk, then follow the city-led route at your own pace.
cards.short_summary: A guided September Trail Tuesday walk on the Greenway.
cards.evidence_claim: The city lists a Trail Tuesday walk on the South Bethlehem Greenway and states Trail Tuesday is free for all residents.
cards.access_notes: Seasonal first-Tuesday program; waiver required. The city specifies it is free for residents, and minors need a parent or guardian.

cards.title: Watch or ride at Bethlehem Skateplaza
cards.subtitle: South Bethlehem Greenway
cards.notes: Bring a skateboard, BMX bike, or inline skates if you ride; otherwise use the plaza as a daylight spot to watch and spend time outdoors.
cards.short_summary: A free public skateplaza integrated with the South Bethlehem Greenway.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Bethlehem states that Bethlehem Skateplaza is a public park and is free.
cards.access_notes: Open dawn to dusk according to the city. Bikes, skateboards, and inline skates are permitted; watching is also described as a use of the space.

cards.title: Record something in Studio 11
cards.subtitle: Bethlehem Area Public Library Main Library
cards.notes: Reserve the self-serve recording studio, bring a USB drive or cloud-storage access for files, and plan your session within Main Library hours.
cards.short_summary: A free recording studio resource for BAPL members.
cards.evidence_claim: Bethlehem Area Public Library states that Studio 11 is a free resource for library members.
cards.access_notes: Library membership is required; the studio is self-serve and uses Main Library hours. Save work to cloud storage or a USB drive.

cards.title: Attend a BAPL Coolidge program
cards.subtitle: BAPL Coolidge, 2740 Fifth Street
cards.notes: Check the library's event listing, select an all-ages program, and arrive during the Coolidge building's posted public hours for a no-cost activity.
cards.short_summary: Free, all-ages programming at BAPL's Coolidge location.
cards.evidence_claim: Bethlehem Area Public Library says BAPL Coolidge hosts free library programs for all ages.
cards.access_notes: Programs vary by calendar. Posted building hours are Tuesday through Thursday and the second Saturday of each month.

cards.title: Visit the Moravian Museum on Free Sunday
cards.subtitle: 66 West Church Street
cards.notes: Choose an eligible first Sunday, reserve ahead if attending the family craft, and explore the museum alongside the scheduled hands-on activity.
cards.short_summary: Free-Sunday museum access with a family craft activity.
cards.evidence_claim: Historic Bethlehem Museums & Sites offers complimentary admission to the Moravian Museum of Bethlehem on designated Free Sundays.
cards.access_notes: Free Sundays run on the first Sunday of February through November, except April's second Sunday. Advance registration for the family craft is requested and limited to families attending with children.

cards.title: Visit Kemerer on Free Sunday
cards.subtitle: 427 North New Street
cards.notes: Plan for an eligible Free Sunday, reserve ahead when joining the family craft, and make time for both the museum galleries and the activity.
cards.short_summary: A designated free-admission Sunday at Kemerer Museum.
cards.evidence_claim: Historic Bethlehem Museums & Sites offers complimentary admission to the Kemerer Museum of Decorative Arts on designated Free Sundays.
cards.access_notes: Free Sundays run on the first Sunday of February through November, except April's second Sunday. Advance registration for the family craft is requested and limited to families attending with children.

cards.title: See the Grist Miller's House on Free Sunday
cards.subtitle: 457 Old York Road
cards.notes: Select a Free Sunday date, reserve ahead if your family will take part in the craft, and combine the restored house visit with the scheduled activity.
cards.short_summary: A restored historic house included in free Sunday admission.
cards.evidence_claim: Historic Bethlehem Museums & Sites includes the 1782 / 1834 Grist Miller's House in its complimentary-admission Free Sundays.
cards.access_notes: Free Sundays run on the first Sunday of February through November, except April's second Sunday. Advance registration for the family craft is requested and limited to families attending with children.

warnings: Several city programs are designated free specifically for City of Bethlehem residents; confirm residency eligibility before registering.
Historic Bethlehem's Free Sunday family craft reservations are limited to families attending with children.

boards.title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
boards.description: Ten documented study settings in and around Reeves Library, from reservable rooms to quiet seating and media-production space.

cards.title: Reeves Library
cards.subtitle: North Campus
cards.notes: Start at the reference desk, then choose a table, carrel, lounge seat, group area, or study room based on the work you need to finish.
cards.short_summary: A central library building with multiple documented study formats.
cards.evidence_claim: Moravian states that Reeves Library provides study tables, individual carrels, group study areas, lounge seating, and study rooms.
cards.access_notes: Located at the heart of North Campus; use the library’s current hours page before visiting.

cards.title: Reeves Library Glass Study Rooms
cards.subtitle: Reeves Library, main floor
cards.notes: Use the glass rooms when your session benefits from a door, whiteboard, and movable tables and chairs; coordinate with collaborators before settling in.
cards.short_summary: Enclosed library rooms configured for individual or group work.
cards.evidence_claim: Moravian documents glass study spaces in Reeves Library with whiteboards and movable tables and chairs for students to meet, collaborate, and study.
cards.access_notes: The source places these rooms in Reeves Library; availability is not stated, so confirm locally.

cards.title: Reeves Library Individual Carrels
cards.subtitle: Reeves Library
cards.notes: Choose an individual carrel for a more self-contained reading or writing session, and ask library staff if you need help locating a suitable seat.
cards.short_summary: Individual workstations among Reeves Library’s study options.
cards.evidence_claim: Moravian lists individual carrels among the study spaces available at Reeves Library.
cards.access_notes: The source identifies carrels as library study space; it does not specify assignment rules for standard carrels.

cards.title: Reeves Library Group Study Areas
cards.subtitle: Reeves Library
cards.notes: Bring your project group to the library’s designated group-study seating and plan your materials before you arrive so the work session can begin promptly.
cards.short_summary: Shared seating areas intended for collaborative academic work.
cards.evidence_claim: Moravian lists group study areas as part of Reeves Library’s study space.
cards.access_notes: Located in Reeves Library; no reservation procedure is stated for these open group areas.

cards.title: Reeves Library Lounge Seating
cards.subtitle: Reeves Library
cards.notes: Use the lounge seating when you want a less desk-like place to read or review; keep headphones handy if your task needs quiet focus.
cards.short_summary: Library lounge seating offered alongside tables and carrels.
cards.evidence_claim: Moravian lists lounge seating among the study spaces at Reeves Library.
cards.access_notes: Located in Reeves Library; the source does not identify a particular floor or availability rules.

cards.title: REEVE 212 Group Study Classroom
cards.subtitle: Reeves Library
cards.notes: For a group session that needs a defined room, look up REEVE 212 in the University’s 25Live booking system before making plans.
cards.short_summary: A group-study classroom listed as reservable through 25Live.
cards.evidence_claim: Moravian’s Reeves Library portal lists REEVE 212 as a group study classroom available through 25Live room bookings.
cards.access_notes: Listed in 25Live room bookings; consult that system for current reservation eligibility and availability.

cards.title: REEVE 315 Group Study Room
cards.subtitle: Reeves Library
cards.notes: Book REEVE 315 when your group needs a television for shared viewing, and verify the reservation details in 25Live before heading over.
cards.short_summary: A reservable group-study room with a television.
cards.evidence_claim: Moravian’s Reeves Library portal lists REEVE 315 as a group study room with television available through 25Live room bookings.
cards.access_notes: Listed in 25Live room bookings; consult that system for current reservation eligibility and availability.

cards.title: Zinczenko New Media Center
cards.subtitle: Reeves Library, lower level
cards.notes: Use this named media-creation space when an assignment involves audio, video, digital, or print work; confirm room scheduling before a production session.
cards.short_summary: A library media center combining a study lounge with media creation.
cards.evidence_claim: Moravian identifies the Zinczenko New Media Center in Reeves Library as a study lounge and media-creation space.
cards.access_notes: Listed through 25Live as REEVE ZNMC; check that system for current scheduling details.

cards.title: Debra Gaspar Reading Nook
cards.subtitle: Reeves Library north bay window-seat area
cards.notes: Take a reading assignment to the nook near the children’s section, where comfortable seating, window cushions, and a bestseller shelf are documented.
cards.short_summary: A named, comfortable reading area in the library’s north bay.
cards.evidence_claim: Moravian describes the Debra Gaspar Reading Nook in Reeves Library’s north bay window-seat area with comfortable seating, custom cushions, and a bookshelf.
cards.source_title: Debra Gaspar Reading Nook | Moravian University
cards.access_notes: Located by the children’s section in Reeves Library; use current library hours when planning a visit.

cards.entity_name: Reeves Library Lower-Level Digital Collaboration Space
cards.title: Reeves Library Digital Collaboration Space
cards.subtitle: Reeves Library, lower level
cards.notes: Set up a multimodal project here when you need screen sharing, movable furniture, movable whiteboards, or a recording studio nearby.
cards.short_summary: A flexible lower-level setting for collaborative digital projects.
cards.evidence_claim: Moravian states that Reeves Library’s lower level has digital collaboration spaces with screen-sharing monitors, movable furniture, and movable whiteboards.
cards.access_notes: Located on the library’s lower level; the source does not state reservation or access requirements.

boards.title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
boards.description: Named historic and cultural destinations on Bethlehem corridors near Moravian University.

cards.title: Read the 1741 Gemeinhaus
cards.subtitle: West Church Street corridor
cards.notes: Walk the West Church Street corridor to the 1741 Gemeinhaus and use the museum’s exhibits to orient yourself to early Bethlehem.
cards.short_summary: A National Historic Landmark housed in Bethlehem’s oldest building.
cards.evidence_claim: Historic Bethlehem identifies the Moravian Museum as located in the 1741 Gemeinhaus, the oldest building in Bethlehem.
cards.source_title: Museums & Sites | Historic Bethlehem Museums & Sites
cards.access_notes: 66 West Church Street; check the museum’s current hours and admission information before entering.

cards.title: See a World Heritage building
cards.subtitle: West Church Street corridor
cards.notes: Pause along West Church Street to view the preserved Single Sisters’ House, then check Historic Bethlehem for any tour or exhibit access.
cards.short_summary: A preserved component of the Moravian Church Settlements–Bethlehem World Heritage site.
cards.evidence_claim: Historic Bethlehem states that the Single Sisters’ House is part of the Moravian Church Settlements–Bethlehem World Heritage Inscription.
cards.source_title: Single Sisters' House | Historic Bethlehem Museums & Sites
cards.access_notes: 50 West Church Street; Historic Bethlehem lists access as custom tours available.

cards.title: Browse three centuries of design
cards.subtitle: North New Street corridor
cards.notes: Follow North New Street to the Kemerer and look for current galleries, period rooms, and changing decorative-arts exhibitions.
cards.short_summary: Museum galleries and period rooms inside three connected nineteenth-century homes.
cards.evidence_claim: Historic Bethlehem says the Kemerer Museum has changing exhibits, period rooms, and galleries covering three centuries of decorative arts.
cards.source_title: Kemerer Museum Admission | Historic Bethlehem Museums & Sites
cards.access_notes: 427 North New Street; ticket availability and current hours should be checked before visiting.

cards.title: Watch for blacksmithing programs
cards.subtitle: Main Street corridor
cards.notes: Use Main Street to reach the 1750 Smithy and check the day’s schedule for demonstrations or other listed programs before you go.
cards.short_summary: A functioning historic smithy interpreting colonial metalworking.
cards.evidence_claim: Historic Bethlehem describes the 1750 Smithy as a functioning site focused on the art of metalworking.
cards.source_title: Museums & Sites | Historic Bethlehem Museums & Sites
cards.access_notes: 425 Main Street; the institution publishes current site hours and program information.

cards.title: Find the historic compounding hearth
cards.subtitle: Main Street corridor
cards.notes: Head down Main Street to the Apothecary and consult Historic Bethlehem about a custom tour to see its preserved laboratory story.
cards.short_summary: A World Heritage-site apothecary with its original 1752 compounding hearth intact.
cards.evidence_claim: Historic Bethlehem reports that the Apothecary’s original 1752 compounding hearth remains intact inside the structure.
cards.access_notes: 418 Main Street; Historic Bethlehem lists custom tours as available.

cards.title: Start with local orientation
cards.subtitle: Main Street corridor
cards.notes: Use the Main Street welcome center to pick up visitor information and confirm which historic sites or tours are open that day.
cards.short_summary: Historic-house welcome center for tickets, visitor information, and tours.
cards.evidence_claim: Historic Bethlehem states that the Goundie House Welcome Center sells museum admission and tour tickets and provides visitor information.
cards.source_title: 1810 Goundie House Welcome Center | Historic Bethlehem Museums & Sites
cards.access_notes: 501 Main Street; consult the official page for the current daily schedule.

cards.title: Browse locally made goods
cards.subtitle: Main Street corridor
cards.notes: Make a Main Street stop for foods, gifts, and handmade products by local artists; purchases support historic-site preservation.
cards.short_summary: A historic-inspired shop carrying local artists’ handmade products.
cards.evidence_claim: Historic Bethlehem says the Schropp Dry Goods Shoppe offers foods, gifts, and handmade products created by local artists.
cards.access_notes: 505 Main Street; this is a retail stop, so purchases are optional.

cards.title: Locate a rare Indigenous-built home
cards.subtitle: Heckewelder Place corridor
cards.notes: Walk Heckewelder Place to view the Nain-Schober House and check Historic Bethlehem’s schedule if you want guided interpretation.
cards.short_summary: An extant eighteenth-century building built by and lived in by Indigenous people in eastern Pennsylvania.
cards.evidence_claim: Historic Bethlehem identifies the Nain-Schober House as the only extant eighteenth-century building built by and lived in by Indigenous people in eastern Pennsylvania.
cards.source_title: Museums & Sites | Historic Bethlehem Museums & Sites
cards.access_notes: 429 Heckewelder Place; Historic Bethlehem lists custom tours as available.

cards.title: Follow the creekside industrial story
cards.subtitle: Ohio Road corridor
cards.notes: Take Ohio Road to the Colonial Industrial Quarter and walk the grounds during its listed dawn-to-dusk access window.
cards.short_summary: Creekside historic landscape interpreting early Bethlehem mills, crafts, and trades.
cards.evidence_claim: Historic Bethlehem says the Colonial Industrial Quarter used spring water and Monocacy Creek waterpower for mills, craftsmen, and trades.
cards.access_notes: 145 Ohio Road; Historic Bethlehem lists the grounds as open dawn to dusk.

cards.title: Connect with local archives
cards.subtitle: Old York Road corridor
cards.notes: Follow Old York Road to the Luckenbach Mill and contact Historic Bethlehem ahead if you need to use its library or archives.
cards.short_summary: Historic mill location that also houses local-history research resources.
cards.evidence_claim: Historic Bethlehem states that its library and archives are located at the Luckenbach Mill at 459 Old York Road.
cards.access_notes: 459 Old York Road; contact Historic Bethlehem for research access arrangements.

boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Ten documented Moravian University traditions, from the North-to-South campus walk to candlelit holiday music and service-centered gatherings.

cards.title: Walk the Moravian Mile
cards.subtitle: Orientation walk between North and South campuses
cards.notes: Join the first-year orientation walk from North to South Campus through Historic Bethlehem; save the reverse route for the senior Backwards Walk.
cards.short_summary: A roughly 0.8-mile campus-to-campus rite of passage.
cards.evidence_claim: Moravian identifies the approximately 0.8-mile North-to-South route as the Moravian Mile and says first-year students traditionally walk it during orientation.
cards.source_title: History of One of America’s Oldest Colleges
cards.access_notes: Scheduled as part of new-student orientation; use the University’s current orientation schedule for participation details.

cards.title: Return on the Backwards Walk
cards.subtitle: Senior reverse walk on the Moravian Mile
cards.notes: If you are a graduating senior, look for the Backwards Walk and retrace the Moravian Mile from South Campus back toward North Campus.
cards.short_summary: Graduates reverse their first-year campus walk.
cards.evidence_claim: Moravian states that graduating seniors take the Backwards Walk, walking the Moravian Mile in reverse after completing their time at the University.
cards.source_title: History of One of America’s Oldest Colleges
cards.access_notes: A graduation-related tradition; confirm current senior-program timing with University communications.

cards.title: Serve on Heritage Day
cards.subtitle: Fall day of heritage learning and community service
cards.notes: Sign up for a local nonprofit service assignment and use the day to connect Moravian’s history with present-day Bethlehem community needs.
cards.short_summary: A fall service day centered on Moravian heritage and community.
cards.evidence_claim: Moravian describes Heritage Day as an annual fall celebration of Moravian tradition, community, and service that includes learning about founders and serving the community.
cards.source_title: History of One of America’s Oldest Colleges
cards.access_notes: Participation locations and sign-up details vary by year; check the Center for Career and Civic Engagement’s event information.

cards.title: Light Up Christmas Vespers
cards.subtitle: Candlelight worship and student music in Bethlehem
cards.notes: Attend respectfully for the student music, Singstunde, and candlelight service; check the annual Vespers page for the current program and access details.
cards.short_summary: Moravian’s candlelit holiday service blends music with two Moravian worship forms.
cards.evidence_claim: Moravian says Christmas Vespers combines student music with the Singstunde and Candlelight Service traditions of the Moravian Church.
cards.access_notes: Held in the holiday season; consult the University’s annual Vespers information for current dates, location, and any access instructions.

cards.title: Mark Founder’s Day
cards.subtitle: University history gathering with Lovefeast and artifacts
cards.notes: Watch for the annual program, then take time with the stories and artifacts that connect today’s campus to Moravian’s early founders.
cards.short_summary: An annual remembrance program built around Moravian history.
cards.evidence_claim: Moravian states that Founder’s Day includes a reception, Lovefeast, luncheon, and stories and artifacts from the University’s past.
cards.source_title: History of One of America’s Oldest Colleges
cards.access_notes: Annual program details may change; check University event announcements before attending.

cards.title: Share a Moravian Lovefeast
cards.subtitle: Orientation community-building gathering
cards.notes: Join the orientation Lovefeast when offered, listen for its community-building context, and follow staff guidance for the shared food and program.
cards.short_summary: A Moravian community-building gathering included in orientation programming.
cards.evidence_claim: Moravian’s transfer orientation materials list a Moravian Lovefeast and describe it as part of a 300-year-old tradition of Moravian community building.
cards.access_notes: Offered through orientation programming when scheduled; confirm whether it appears in the current orientation itinerary.

cards.title: Take a Finals-Eve Oasis
cards.subtitle: Midnight breakfast at the Star and Clewell Dining Hall
cards.notes: During finals, check the campus schedule for Midnight Oasis and head to the Star or Clewell Dining Hall for the named midnight breakfast.
cards.short_summary: A finals-period midnight breakfast with a distinctly Moravian name.
cards.evidence_claim: Moravian’s new-student terminology guide defines Midnight Oasis as a midnight breakfast in the Star and Clewell Dining Hall during finals.
cards.access_notes: Occurs during finals; confirm the current dining and event schedule for date, meal-plan use, and access.

cards.title: Cheer at Powderpuff
cards.subtitle: Fall sorority flag-football competition
cards.notes: Attend as a spectator or, if eligible through a participating chapter, follow the event’s team and safety instructions for the fall flag-football games.
cards.short_summary: Sorority teams compete through a fall football bracket.
cards.evidence_claim: Moravian says its fall Powderpuff Football Game features sorority-member teams, student coaches, and a final game that names a Powderpuff Champion.
cards.access_notes: Fall event; participation is tied to teams and chapter eligibility, while spectators should follow the current event notice.

cards.title: See Greek God & Goddess
cards.subtitle: Late-fall talent and question-and-answer contest
cards.notes: Catch the late-fall program to see chapter representatives take part in the talent and question-and-answer contest judged by University administrators.
cards.short_summary: A chapter-representative contest that supports selected philanthropies.
cards.evidence_claim: Moravian describes Greek God & Goddess as a late-fall contest with talent and question-and-answer components, selecting one fraternity member and one sorority member.
cards.access_notes: Late-fall event; representative participation is chapter-based, so consult the current Greek Life schedule for audience access.

cards.title: Watch the Turkey Bowl
cards.subtitle: Pre-Thanksgiving flag football at John Makuvek Field
cards.notes: Before Thanksgiving Break, follow the current IFC announcement to watch the fraternity teams compete for the Turkey Bowl championship at John Makuvek Field.
cards.short_summary: A pre-break fraternity flag-football tournament.
cards.evidence_claim: Moravian states that the Inter-Fraternity Council sponsors a pre-Thanksgiving flag football tournament at John Makuvek Field for the Turkey Bowl championship.
cards.access_notes: Scheduled before Thanksgiving Break; team participation is fraternity-based, and spectators should consult the current event notice.

boards.title: Your First Weekend at Moravian University, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A low-pressure, under-21-safe sequence that starts on North Campus and finishes with walkable Bethlehem history.

cards.title: 1. Get oriented on the Quad
cards.subtitle: Main Street Campus · first daylight stop
cards.notes: Start with a slow lap through the Quad, then use the surrounding buildings as landmarks before choosing a study or student-life stop.
cards.short_summary: A simple first look at the center of everyday North Campus activity.
cards.evidence_claim: Moravian identifies the Quad on North Campus as a place where students spend time, attend events, and participate in clubs and activities.
cards.access_notes: Located on Moravian’s Main Street (North) Campus; use the campus map to orient yourself.

cards.title: 2. Choose a study corner at Reeves
cards.subtitle: Main Street Campus · reset with your class materials
cards.notes: Bring a syllabus or reading list and test a study setup that fits you: carrel, group area, lounge seating, or a glass study room.
cards.short_summary: A practical early stop for learning the campus’s main study resource.
cards.evidence_claim: Reeves Library provides study space for more than 400 students, including glass study rooms, carrels, group areas, and lounge seating.
cards.access_notes: Library access and service availability can vary; check the library’s current hours before going.

cards.title: 3. Find the New Media Center
cards.subtitle: Reeves Library · make a note for future projects
cards.notes: Locate the New Media Center while you are already in Reeves so you know where to ask about audio or video work later in the term.
cards.short_summary: A quick reconnaissance stop for students who may need media-production space.
cards.evidence_claim: Moravian states that Reeves Library houses the Zinczenko New Media Center, including a video and audio recording studio.
cards.access_notes: Confirm equipment access, reservations, and staff availability with Reeves Library.

cards.title: 4. Learn the HUB layout
cards.subtitle: 1119 Monocacy Street · student-life hub
cards.notes: Walk through the HUB and save the information desk, Student Life suite, dining areas, and organization spaces as useful landmarks for the semester.
cards.short_summary: A central stop for finding services and campus connection points.
cards.evidence_claim: Moravian describes the HUB as a central gathering space that regularly hosts events, meetings, and programs and contains student services and dining.
cards.source_title: New Student Guide to Campus Life | Moravian University
cards.access_notes: The HUB is at 1119 Monocacy Street; specific offices and services may have separate availability.

cards.title: 5. Have a meal at the Star
cards.subtitle: HUB · plan around your dining access
cards.notes: Use a meal break to notice the HUB dining flow, then check the posted options and ask dining staff about navigating any dietary needs.
cards.short_summary: A campus meal stop integrated into the HUB rather than a separate trip.
cards.evidence_claim: Moravian identifies the Star, located in the HUB, as its largest dining room and includes it among new-student dining options.
cards.access_notes: Dining availability and payment options depend on current dining operations and your plan or account.

cards.title: 6. Check out the Doghouse
cards.subtitle: Moravian campus · weekday community space
cards.notes: On a weekday, bring your ID and use a short visit to see whether this community space could work for studying, relaxing, or meeting classmates.
cards.short_summary: A low-key campus space intended for current Moravian community members.
cards.evidence_claim: Moravian’s event policies describe the Doghouse as a community programming space accessible to current students on weekdays from 8 a.m. to 6 p.m. with an active ID.
cards.access_notes: Current Moravian students need an active University ID for weekday entry; the published access window is Monday–Friday, 8 a.m.–6 p.m.

cards.title: 7. Find Borhek Chapel
cards.subtitle: Comenius Hall · note it for campus programs
cards.notes: Locate the chapel from the north end of Comenius Hall and check campus communications for any public program that matches your interest.
cards.short_summary: A historic campus venue used for an array of University-sponsored programs.
cards.evidence_claim: Moravian says Borhek Chapel is at the north end of Comenius Hall and may be used during the academic year by University organizations.
cards.access_notes: The chapel is reservable; access depends on the scheduled program or organizer.

cards.title: 8. Add South Campus to your map
cards.subtitle: Priscilla Payne Hurd Campus · music and art area
cards.notes: Walk or travel to South Campus in daylight, find Foy Concert Hall, and keep it in mind when scanning future music and arts announcements.
cards.short_summary: A named performance venue on Moravian’s historic South Campus.
cards.evidence_claim: Moravian identifies the Priscilla Payne Hurd Campus as home to its music and art departments and lists Foy Concert Hall there.
cards.access_notes: Concert-hall entry depends on scheduled events or reservations; check the event listing before returning for a performance.

cards.title: 9. Browse the Moravian Book Shop
cards.subtitle: 428 Main Street · Historic Downtown Bethlehem
cards.notes: Take a daylight stroll to Main Street, browse the student bookstore section, and use the posted hours to plan a return if you need course supplies.
cards.short_summary: A downtown bookstore that also serves as Moravian University’s student bookstore.
cards.evidence_claim: Historic Bethlehem identifies the Moravian Book Shop at 428 Main Street as home to the Moravian University student bookstore.
cards.source_title: Moravian Book Shop | Visit Historic Bethlehem
cards.access_notes: The source lists daily public retail hours; purchases are optional.

cards.title: 10. End at the Colonial Industrial Quarter
cards.subtitle: 145 Ohio Road · outdoor historic grounds
cards.notes: Finish with a daylight walk through the grounds and along the creek; treat building interiors and any ticketed programming as separate plans.
cards.short_summary: An outdoor historic-site walk near downtown Bethlehem and the Monocacy Creek.
cards.evidence_claim: Historic Bethlehem states that the Colonial Industrial Quarter grounds at 145 Ohio Road are open daily from dawn to dusk.
cards.source_title: Colonial Industrial Quarter | Historic Bethlehem Museums & Sites
cards.access_notes: The grounds are open dawn to dusk; consult the site for specific building hours and ticketed-program details.
